newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Kinkel rules out sending German troops to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel rules out sending German troops to Albania.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Saturday dimissed any notion of his country sending troops to Albania, warning against hasty, ill-thought-out intervention.
"German soldiers will not go into Albania," Kinkel told reporters, using the strongest language yet to underline Bonn's position.
"We can't get involved in another adventure," he said.
Kinkel was speaking on the margins of a European Union foreign ministers meeting at which divisions had emerged among the European countries over possible intervention in Albania.
The EU was ready to offer humanitarian assistance, he said, but the Albanians had to put down their weapons and clear entry into their ports.
Drawing a parallel with the West's efforts in former Yugoslavia, Kinkel said no one should rush in to Albania without being clear what they needed to do.
"If there is one consequence you can draw from Yugoslavia, it is that you cannot send one soldier or one policeman without a crystal-clear mandate," he said.
He also dismissed criticism that the international community was again sitting helpless while a country burned.
"Something happens in Albania and two or three days later it is said 'why isn't it solved yet?," he said.
Kinkel refused to join the growing chorus calling for Albanian President Sali Berisha to step down.
"If there is to be a political solution, the president will have to consider when and how he can contribute to a solution," he said.
